speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Before we proceed with the next Motion, I wish to state for the record that at the General Election held on 11 September 2015, Ms Lee Li Lian of the Workers' Party was declared by the Returning Officer as the candidate elected as a Non-Constituency Member of Parliament (NCMP) in accordance with section 52 of the Parliamentary Elections Act.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Low, please move your Motion and make your speech.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Ms Lee Li Lian has not taken the Oath of Allegiance under Article 61 of the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore at the first Sitting on 15 January 2016 and the second Sitting on 25 January 2016 of the First session of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Under the Parliamentary Elections Act, three NCMP seats were declared elected.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Since Ms Lee Li Lian has not taken up the seat, Parliament has the power to resolve to fill the vacant seat.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, there were only three NCMP seats declared under the Act at the last General Election.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Workers' Party believes that the NCMP scheme is not the way forward to make our political system more robust.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The NCMP scheme has become an attempt to whitewash the tremendous negative impact driven by the change in our political system from Single Member Constituency (SMC) to the creation of GRCs to entrench a one-party political system with no insurance against the failure of the Ruling party.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Workers' Party is a rational and responsible political party.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: We understand that the struggle for a functional democracy by a loyal Opposition must be fought from within the existing system under the law legislated by Parliament even though we disagree with that.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Therefore, we do not oppose individual Members who are willing to sacrifice their time and energy to contribute to the national debate in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Hence, if one Member who is declared as NCMP is unable to take up the seat, it is my duty as the leader of the Workers' Party to nominate the next best volunteer.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: This is why I have decided to move the Motion.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Constitution of the Republic of Singapore provides us for a maximum of nine NCMPs from the Opposition in this House if there are none being elected at the January elections.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: When the NCMP scheme was proposed in 1984, three benefits were given in support of the scheme.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: These purported benefits were repeated again in 2010 when NCMP seats were increased from six to nine seats.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The first reason is to provide PAP Ministers and Members with the experience of the cut and thrust of debate by sparring with Opposition Members.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The second reason is to allow the electorate to judge for themselves what elected Opposition Members can and cannot do for the people.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The third reason is to dispel any suspicions of cover-ups, since Opposition Members would give vent to any allegation of misfeasance or corruption or nepotism, even if these proved false and allow the Government to rebut them.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: From the above, Mdm Speaker, it is clear that the creation of the NCMP scheme is chiefly for the benefit of the Ruling party and Opposition Members are deemed as valuable only in relation to the training they give the PAP Ministers and Members.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Although the PAP is trying very hard to convince Singaporeans that NCMPs are on par with elected Members, they have shown the cloven hoof by referring to the NCMPs as second-class Members in this House and Opposition best losers who crave for publicity and personal fame.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Such a view was characteristically articulated two days ago in this House by Member Cedric Foo who was so arrogant to say that Mr Leon Perera's presence here is by the grace of the PAP.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It is the view of the Workers' Party that the only way forward for a strong Parliament, one that can hold the government of the day to account, is for the Ruling party, in the position of strength, to create a political system that would allow both genuine and loyal Opposition parties to grow as well as the Ruling party to perform and compete for seats.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I expect the Workers' Party's NCMPs to grow strong from their position of weakness and to hold their heads up high with pride and dignity.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: They will respect Parliament, respect the law and respect themselves.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I remember, in particular, her speaking passionately during the Population White Paper debate in 2013.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: She had only just entered Parliament then but brought with her a passion for matters she felt strongly about.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: As my opponent in Punggol East SMC in last year's General Election, Ms Lee fought a very good clean fight.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: When the election results were announced, I was happy to note that she qualified for an NCMP position and the residents of Punggol East could benefit from the voice of someone who had worked with them for more than two and a half years.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: But this was short-lived as Ms Lee declared soon afterwards that she would not be taking up the NCMP position.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This was really not for the benefit of the PAP but for the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: So, I am a bit puzzled by Mr Low Thia Khiang's claim that the NCMP scheme is for the benefit of the PAP to provide them with sparring partners.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: If this was so, then why do we get Workers' Party's candidates accepting the position in the first place for the benefit of the PAP?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: While the Workers' Party was initially extremely opposed to the scheme, and some of them may still be opposed to the scheme, their position towards it in recent years appears to have softened somewhat, as they must have come to realise that whatever the shortcomings they perceived the scheme has, it does actually confer benefits on members of the Opposition parties.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I say "appears" because we have received mixed signals from the leadership of the Workers' Party, with Mr Low Thia Khiang being on record as saying that he would resign from his Party if it is insisted that he takes up an NCMP seat.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: On the other hand, members of the Workers' Party, who have previously been NCMPs, have spoken positively of their experience.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: But we are not here to debate the inconsistencies in the Workers' Party's position or what their internal politics are.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: There is a more important issue which this House needs to consider.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Where there is a framework within which we must work, everyone involved should respect it and not try to find ways to game the system.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This applies across the board regardless of party affiliation or political inclinations.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: We would be very disappointed if Ms Lee's decision to decline the NCMP position was supported by her party for that reason.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: It would be a rather unfortunate misuse of the guarantee in the Constitution that at least nine Opposition Members of Parliament will be offered places in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: My experience with having an NCMP working in my previous constituency was a very positive one.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Although Mr Yee Jenn Jong was, as the title suggests, a Non-constituency Member, his presence in this House gave residents of Joo Chiat SMC an additional voice in Parliament, which was only natural as he was closely in touch with issues in Joo Chiat.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: For example, when there was a serious dengue outbreak in Joo Chiat, while I worked the ground with the grassroots leaders and NEA officers, Mr Yee raised this issue in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Although we were political rivals during the Elections, I believe that we were more interested in working for the good of residents after the Elections, notwithstanding our different party colours.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I commend Mr Yee for this and I thank him for his commitment to residents of Joo Chiat while I was the serving Member of Parliament there.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: To come back to Ms Lee's reason for declining the seat, which I mentioned earlier, I do not think that Mr Yee's decision to take up the NCMP position was in anyway disrespectful of the decision of the majority.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: On the contrary, it was a benefit to all residents in Joo Chiat SMC.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: He is an example of an NCMP who sought to grow his roots in the constituency that he had contested in and I certainly do not consider him to be anything like duckweed, without roots; or a vase only for show.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Both descriptions do him and the work that he has done a great disservice.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: It would be like allowing me, after having won the Election in Punggol East, to decline my seat in Parliament and instead pass it on to the PAP candidate who stood in Aljunied GRC or Hougang SMC.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This is not something we permit for constituency Members of Parliament, so we need to review whether this is something which makes sense for NCMPs.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: For example, it would be useful to understand if the Workers' Party would support a transfer where the next best loser was not a Workers' Party candidate but a candidate from another Opposition party.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I agree with the Prime Minister this is, on the whole, beneficial in providing a diversity of views, contributes to more considered debates and, therefore, beneficial for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: So, I welcome the amendments to the NCMP scheme proposed by the Government, and in respect of the Motion being debated, I believe the House would be worse off with one fewer Opposition Member contributing to debates and deliberations.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: However, I do think that it is unfortunate that Ms Lee Li Lian has decided not to accept the seat even though she was the first best loser in the 2015 General Elections.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I have nothing against the Workers' Party's prospective candidate for the vacated NCMP seat.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: But I feel it is a point which bears further consideration.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Normally, I do not like to criticise the Opposition party, but this time, I really have to get it off my chest.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Workers' Party (WP) has always insisted that, in principle, they object to the NCMP scheme.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They said that if the Government did away with the GRC system, then there would be more Opposition Members in Parliament and we would not need the NCMP scheme.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Let us not debate for now whether this is true or not.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I just want to remind all Members, as the Prime Minister said two days ago, that the objective of the GRC system was to ensure enough non-Chinese Members in Parliament to defend our multiracial and multicultural spirit and to ensure that the minorities are not marginalised.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, WP has the right to uphold a principle that is different from PAP's.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But the problem is that, when facing an NCMP seat, WP members have a different attitude.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: WP's Secretary-General Mr Low Thia Khiang said in Parliament in 2010 that he would never accept an NCMP seat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If WP forces him to take up the NCMP seat, he would rather resign, but whether or not other WP members should accept the NCMP seat is up to the Party's decision.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: WP's Chairman, Ms Sylvia Lim, said in 2009 that this scheme was, in her own words, "overall supportable".

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: She said that Singapore's election system is a first-past-the-post system, which can easily result in a situation whereby one party takes up an overwhelming majority of the seats.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, the NCMP scheme can allow the people who have voted for the Opposition to be represented in Parliament.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If you think these words sound familiar, then you are right!

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is the exact reason why the Government implemented the NCMP scheme.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim accepted the NCMP seat in 2006.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Back then, she said that since there were more than 50,000 voters in Aljunied GRC who had voted for WP, she felt that she had the obligation to accept the NCMP seat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It looks like WP is saying one thing yet doing another when it comes to the NCMP seat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Two days ago, we even heard Mr Low Thia Khiang referring NCMPs as "the duckweeds in a pond".

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Today, however, he is moving a Motion to bring another piece of "duckweed" into Parliament; or, to "float" into Parliament.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I do not understand what the real stance of the WP is!

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If it is indeed like what Mr Low has said, that the NCMP scheme only benefits the PAP or the Ruling party, then why bother bringing another NCMP into Parliament?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Even if we accept that the WP regards the NCMP scheme as an interim measure, there is, however, a WP member who has gone against this stance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Ms Lee Li Lian has refused to take up this seat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that she has her own considerations.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, before the election, the WP should have ensured that all the candidates were prepared to abide by the Constitution and our political system to serve the voters.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: No candidates should have this attitude that they will serve the voters only if they are elected.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The WP has failed to do so and I am very disappointed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think this is not a reasonable request.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Let us compare an NCMP with an elected MP.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Just like my Parliamentary colleague, Mr Charles Chong, has mentioned: if any elected Member of Parliament cannot fulfil his duty for some reasons, the seat cannot be transferred.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If it is an SMC, then according to our Constitution, the seat must be filled through by-election to elect another Member.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Back then, Ms Lee Li Lian was elected into Parliament through a by-election.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: To be fair, the NCMP seat should also not be transferable.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If Ms Lee Li Lian did not decline this seat, there would have been nine Opposition Members.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In the future, there will be at least 12 Opposition Members.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, an NCMP will have the same voting rights as an elected Member, which means that they will be able to influence national policies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The NCMP scheme is already written into our Constitution.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The system ensures that, regardless of the election results, in constituencies where the vote shares are very close, the Opposition parties will have the chance to represent their voters in Parliament.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, only the losers who garnered the highest vote share can be qualified as an NCMP.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This scheme should not become something like a proportional representation, to allow the party with the second highest vote share to have a certain quota to nominate their candidates.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If we change the NCMP scheme into proportional representation to a certain extent, will it be constitutional?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The percentage of votes garnered by the WP in Punggol East was almost 9% higher than that in the East Coast GRC.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, the WP is now proposing to transfer the Parliament representation entitled by the Punggol East voters to East Coast GRC voters.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is this fair to the Punggol East voters?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: WP claimed that they wanted to represent Singaporeans, but does their Motion truly respect the people's will?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope Members can ponder on this carefully.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the WP would be able to clarify this so that the voters will be well-informed in the next election before casting their sacred votes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, Madam, let me refer to Member Charles Chong's earlier speech where he made some comments about being disappointed that Ms Lee Li Lian would not take up the seat and how Punggol East residents would be disappointed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first and most important reason, she cited, was that she had been the incumbent Member of Parliament in Punggol East SMC for two and a half years, and had to respect the voters' collective decision not to re-elect her.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In other words, she had the mandate of the voters of the constituency but it had been lost.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And Madam, contrary to what Mr Charles Chong had earlier said, the Party did not support Ms Lee's decision because we "want to swop candidates".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We respect her decision that she was the incumbent Member of Parliament who had lost and she wanted to give due respect to the voters' collective decision not to re-elect her.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Personally, if I had been in her shoes, I would have done the same.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The next succeeding candidate would be one of the team-mates of NCMP Leon Perera from the East Coast GRC team.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The only time this arose previously was after the 1984 General Election, when it was the Government itself that moved the Motion to fill the vacancy.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, Madam, the Government itself condones the filling of a vacancy when an NCMP does not take up the seat or as Mr Charles Chong and Er Dr Lee had said, the Government condones the "transfer of NCMP seats".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We are moving this Motion today because the Constitution provides for it.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We also recognise that the Workers' Party can make a contribution to the nation this way.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Because what I had said was that the scheme was overall supportable in the context of GRCs and gerrymandering that has been taking place in our political system, which I think I do not have to elaborate on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And I mentioned in Parliament that the Prime Minister was trying to make a bad situation better.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But the NCMP scheme is not the way forward to make the system more robust.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And that was why the Workers' Party voted against the Constitutional amendment in 2010.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Entrenching the NCMP scheme as good politics sends the wrong signal.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To Singaporeans, the signal being sent is having Opposition voices is enough.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At that election, the PAP faced a national swing that reduced its vote share to 60% and the first loss of a GRC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At the post-election press conference, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong was in a sombre mood.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: He reflected that Singaporeans were concerned with various issues such as the cost of living and housing, education and healthcare, and also with the PAP's approach to Government.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Prime Minister Lee pledged that the PAP would "analyse the results, learn from what has emerged, put right what is wrong, improve what can be made better, and also improve ourselves to serve Singaporeans better." Madam, last year at the state funeral of Mr Lee Kuan Yew, we even learnt that the Prime Minister went into meditation after the 2011 GE.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: However, Singaporeans could not have helped noticing the slew of palpable changes in many unpopular policies after the 2011 GE, including the slaughtering of some sacred cows.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These included reviewing benchmarking Ministerial salaries to top private sector earners, delinking prices of BTO flats from market transactions and putting Government monies into acquiring buses for the use of public transport operators.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In 2013, the PAP lost Punggol East SMC to the Workers' Party, the second blow in two years that made them quicken the pace of change.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Singaporeans forced the PAP to review their policies, at the risk of losing more ground.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If Opposition Members do not manage constituencies, they would not be able to demonstrate that they, too, were up to the task of representing their constituents, building vibrant communities, and, yes, running the Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Should the Ruling party decay or become corrupt, it would be too late to look around for any other party with ground experience, as there may well be none.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Png Eng Huat, are you going to make a clarification?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The PAP then believed that it could define its brand of democracy by allowing up to three Opposition Members in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Mr Dhanabalan simply added that, "the Motion is just to implement the law." Nothing more, nothing less.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: My colleagues in this House have spoken in detail on the Motion so I shall not repeat those points.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It is understandable for some PAP Members in this House to want to take this opportunity to score some political points.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: After all, in the Motion of 1985, Mr Dhanabalan said, and I quote, "politicians are practical people" and that "they look at the practical exercise of influence and power".

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: A distribution of power and influence in this House is so lopsided that the Ruling party can dictate the number of NCMP seats it allows, and at the same time, denying these seats to be filled through its sheer majority.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The Ruling party may say that it has given us three NCMP seats but it is the Workers' Party that created the vacancy.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: But the PAP Government has also enacted the law for such vacancy to be filled in the event that a candidate does not wish to take up the NCMP seat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As the hon Member Er Dr Lee Bee Wah said, none of us, none, would like to see this House criticising each other.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is not the purpose of why we are gathered here.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are gathered in this House because we want to make a difference to the lives of fellow Singaporeans and we want to leave behind a better Singapore for our children and generations to come.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Motion before us goes beyond the procedural issue of filling an empty NCMP seat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Motion that stands before us has far more fundamental implications.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It goes to the heart of the rights and responsibilities of all of us being elected Members of Parliament (MPs), be it MPs or NCMPs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are all elected by the voters into this House, including NCMPs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In response to Mr Low's earlier point, I would be the first to say that if any of my PAP MPs dare call an NCMP a second-class citizen, I, as the Whip, will put them in their place.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But on the other hand, please do not call them duckweeds because even in a pond, duckweeds have a purpose.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us respect the different roles that we play in this House, be it as MPs, NCMPs or Nominated Members of Parliament (NMPs).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We may play different roles but we can all be united by a common purpose to serve Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many Members in this House have spoken, including our Opposition colleagues, and everyone has pointed out that for Singapore to continue to enjoy success, we must continue to have the diversity of perspectives.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must continue to have robust decision-making in this House.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: One of the ways in which this Government has sought to achieve this is through the NCMP scheme where the best losers in a General Election can still enter Parliament, participate in the debates and participate in the decision-making for the good of our country.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Even if a single party today wins all 89 seats in this Parliament, we are assured of nine NCMPs and nine NMPs, by law, for them to join this House to participate in our decision-making.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When we first started this scheme, we started modestly.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To be frank, at that point in time, no one really knew what the future would be like.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Over time, we grew it to six NCMPs and then to nine.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: NCMPs will have the same voting rights although they do not need to look after a constituency.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: NCMPs can continue to contribute to the debates and the decision-making in this House regardless of whether they have a constituency or not.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Why does the Prime Minister, having just led his party to an election where his party won 69% of the votes, want to do this?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Is it for selfish partisan political reasons or is it for something more?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have always said the primary concern, the number one concern for the PAP is the longevity of our country, Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We put that way ahead of the longevity of our own party and we have never changed from that position.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are making these changes because we want to continue to strengthen our political system, not just for this generation, but for many more generations to come.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Is it, as some suggest, for narrow partisan political interest?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If so, why do we need to do it?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Why do we need to do it now?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And there are people on the ground who asked us: why are you doing this?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do not know, but we believe that this is good for Singapore and that is why we are doing it.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This very act is the embrace of debate, not the fear of debate.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: No one should doubt that we are willing to fill the last vacant NCMP seat in this House.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We look forward to having a full and complete House, with MPs, NCMPs and NMPs all vigorously debating the future of our country, working hand-in-hand, for the good of our country.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, we have no trouble at all, supporting a Motion to fill the last NCMP seat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But we do have an issue with the reason that Ms Lee Li Lian gave for giving up her seat in favour of another Workers' Party's candidate.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do have an issue with the Workers' Party's motivation in supporting Ms Lee Li Lian's decision and moving this Motion to declare the seat vacant.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Workers' Party has often spoken up against the NCMP scheme, including in this very House, this very afternoon.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In 2010, Mr Low Thia Khiang too said that, "We will vote against it in-principle because that is not a system we should entrench as a political system." Just on Wednesday, Mr Low Thia Khiang repeated this outside the Chamber and I quote, NCMPs have no "political muscle". "An NCMP is just duckweed on the water of a pond...

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: You don't have roots, unlike elected MPs …" and so on and so forth.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But, the Workers' Party obviously see advantages for itself in accepting NCMP seats.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Because, despite the repeated objections, many Workers' Party candidates have in fact taken up the NCMP seats in the past and in today's Chamber.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In 1988, Dr Lee Siew Choh became the Party's first serving NCMP.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In more recent times, Mr Yee Jenn Jong and Mr Gerald Giam both took up the NCMP seats that were offered to them last term.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Yee said in 2011, and I quote, "It is more effective to be able to have a voice through the NCMP scheme than not".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And they must have found meaning to be able to join the debates in Parliament to contribute to the future of our country.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, Ms Sylvia Lim, Workers' Party Chairman, despite statements to the contrary, has publicly expressed support for the scheme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And the next sentence is even more important.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: She said, "It will also facilitate Opposition parties serving the people in Parliament based on results obtained at General Elections." Mdm Speaker, Members of this House, this is exactly the reason why the Government introduced the scheme and now, to want to strengthen it further.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Lim was once an NCMP as she had shared.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When she accepted her NCMP seat in 2006, Ms Lim said that it was with "that sense of obligation", to those voters who had voted for her, that she was taking up the appointment.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: She said that her decision to accept the seat was made easier because "more than 58,000 people actually wanted a Workers' Party voice for Aljunied GRC".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We welcome both of them as equal Members in this House in debate.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But Ms Lee Li Lian did not accept the seat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many in this House who have spoken in the last few days, including Mr Leon Perera on Tuesday, said that it was a privilege to participate in the debate in this House.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And we all said that we want to serve Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Like her party colleagues, one would have hoped, expected, wished that Ms Lee Li Lian would have the same sense of obligation to do right by the support of the people who had voted for her.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The voters of Punggol East have given Ms Lee Li Lian the right to serve and, I am sure, they look forward to her service to our nation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On the day when Ms Lee lost the election, she said, "I should give this chance to my other Workers' Party colleagues.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We really have some good people who deserve the slot".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The right and the privilege were given to her by Punggol East residents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It was not for her to give it to someone else.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Then, the very next day, Ms Lee repeated a similar sentiment, that "There are better people in the party that we should showcase.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let the people see how good these people are". "Showcase".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The honour and privilege to join this House are for service to our nation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not for us to showcase ourselves.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not for us to showcase our party talents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If we do that, we come in with the wrong end in mind.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And for the third time, on 16 September, Ms Lee said, "The NCMP role is better suited for an aspiring MP who has no such experience and should take this up to show how he or she can contribute in Parliament." Again, "to show".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us remember our duty and responsibility as Members of this House.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us not turn the NCMP scheme into a revolving door to showcase our talent for our own party objectives.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are here to answer a higher calling: to serve Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are not here to showcase our talent.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not like this for the Prime Minister.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not like this for any of the Ministers, any Members of Parliament, including NCMPs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And I hope that we, as Members in this House, will continue to bear this in our hearts as we go forth in our journey to serve Singapore and Singaporeans, first and foremost.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, let me categorically say this again that we want to see the third NCMP seat filled.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Lee Li Lian was the person who qualified.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Daniel Goh is the person that the Workers' Party supports to take up the seat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, clearly, there are advantages to take up the NCMP seat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I do not think people take up the NCMP seat to do the PAP a favour.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Why would you want to do so and be so gracious to train the PAP?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When one takes up the NCMP scheme, I hope it is for the correct reason, to serve Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And I hope it is not for the wrong reason, to showcase your talent.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do not want the NCMP scheme to be a revolving door.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is the reason why I cannot understand the events that happened this week.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I do not know how Mr Leon Perera or Mr Dennis Tan feel.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But I would guarantee you that none of my PAP MPs would ever call you "duckweeds".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, why not let us be honest with each other, as our founding Prime Minister had urged us to be, as Members of this House?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are political merits for any political party to take up the NCMP scheme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And if we say that with a straight face, touch our hearts, I do not think anybody will fault the person for saying it.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We just have to be frank with ourselves, why we do it.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The NCMP scheme must certainly have also benefited the Workers' Party.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If not, why does the Workers' Party allow its members to take up the NCMP seats, not just two, but all three?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If it is just for the PAP, why do it?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And if Ms Lee Li Lian had been upfront, honest about it with her voters before they cast their votes, declare that she is not the best candidate and that even if she gets the highest vote share, she would not take up her NCMP seat, I think the Punggol East residents would feel that they are fairly treated, fairly respected.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Now, if you say that the NCMP scheme does not give any political party muscle, again, the question is: why bother to fill the NCMP seat?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Chan, do you have a copy of the amendment?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Clerks, can you help to distribute copies of the amendment?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Chan, can you please move your amendment?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We look forward to all Members in this House participating robustly in the decision making for the future of our country.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We look forward to having a full and complete House to advance the future of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We also look forward to the day where every candidate who stands for election has in his or her heart the full commitment to serve, regardless as an MP or NCMP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That when we as candidates, when we walk the streets to ask for the votes of our electorate, to canvass for their support, and that when we tell them to place their trust in us, we mean it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When we say that, "Let me be of service to you", we mean it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it does not matter whether we serve as an MP or NCMP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But it matters more than ever that we serve Singapore and Singaporeans and it matters that we respect the will of the voters.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: An NCMP can contribute no less than any MP in this House.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, as I have said, an NCMP without constituency responsibilities should be able to contribute as much, if not much more to Parliament.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: An NCMP has the privilege to demonstrate to Singaporeans his capabilities and commitment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us not turn the NCMP scheme from one of service to the nation into a revolving door for partisan, political, talent displays.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: The Question is, "That the words proposed to be added, be there added." Are there any Members who wish to take the floor?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That narrative is that the Workers' Party are bad people.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is a narrative that is frequently heard.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is that the Workers' Party is shifty, somehow untrustworthy, our motives have to be questioned, our integrity is to be questioned, and that has found expression in the amendment to the Motion that has been tabled before the House.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It has been put across that we are contradictory; we are contradicting ourselves by accepting the NCMP seat and at the same time opposing the NCMP scheme in principle.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I will share my personal perspective and point of view, because I think no doubt that it is relevant.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many people will want to know why it is that I oppose the NCMP scheme in principle, but I have agreed to accept an NCMP position myself.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But before I do so, let me just suggest another consideration to this House which is this: the thrust of People's Action Party Members of this House in speaking on the NCMP scheme – both the current NCMP scheme and the new scheme that is being formed – is that this is, Mdm Speaker, a gesture of magnanimity on the part of the People's Action Party.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is charity that it is being extended, and for which we should be grateful.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That benefit is that the NCMP scheme allows the People's Action Party to send a very strong message to the Singaporean people.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That message is you do not need to vote for any party other than the People's Action Party.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: You should, you ought, you can and you must return 100% of elected Members of Parliament seats to the People's Action Party and you should relegate Opposition parties to NCMP seats.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I can see how that benefits the People's Action Party.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I suspect that that benefit may play out.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think if that message is the message that is put across to the Singaporean electorate and that message is accepted by the Singaporean electorate, what will happen is the negation of the evolution of genuine democracy, real political balance in this country.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And a passion for real political balance and genuine democracy, Mdm Speaker, is not just why I am here.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is why my Workers' Party colleagues are all here.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is 92% or 93% of all parliamentary seats —

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Perera, please keep your speech relevant to the Motion and the amendment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If the hyper majority of the People's Action Party becomes basically unassailable, then the will of the people will not effectively be enforced.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: While we are discussing the NCMP scheme, I note in passing – I know you have said I should limit my speech to the Motion – that we do not have a completely level political playing field here.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Workers' Party has made a number of recommendations on its manifesto on political reforms.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Now it is not the time to go into those in any detail, but I want to note that in passing, we do not have an independent Electoral Commission.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The People's Association does not work with Workers' Party in the same way as the PAP —

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Perera, that is not relevant to the Motion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: It was a very difficult decision to make.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But I decided that on balance, I could make a constructive contribution.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And on balance, I could make a constructive contribution, and that the benefits will outweigh the risk.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I could make a constructive contribution that would help in the longer term cause of political balance in this country.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Whether that was the right decision or not, I will leave that to others to judge, but I think it is something that all of us in the Workers' Party have to continually review as we move forward, whether in the context of a changing political landscape, changing rules, whether this balance and this decision still holds true.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: We are here today to debate this Motion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: We have heard many hon Members of the People's Action Party talk about Ms Lee Li Lian.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: To be very honest, Mdm Speaker, she is not here in this Chamber to defend herself.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Workers' Party Members have attempted to speak out to explain her reasons, but she is not here to defend herself.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: She is not a person who lacks integrity.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: She has worked very, very hard, as some Members have noted.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Even when she was pregnant, she did house visits.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But we are gathered here today to debate this Motion which I think is having the effect of painting a certain narrative about the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Can any member of the People's Action Party provide that answer?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And if I just may be permitted one last point before I resume my seat —

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Do not stray from the Motion, Mr Perera.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: In that case, I will conclude, Mdm Speaker.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang, would you like to summarise and reply?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: She feels that she should not accept because she has lost the mandate to serve Punggol East.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: She was an MP with full mandate to be in this House.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I will deal with that in terms of mandate and what Parliament is for.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I think we better go back to the basics and fundamental.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I think it is what Minister Heng Swee Keat had asked, "What for?" I will go back to that later, but let me deal with the amended Motion first.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The argument that because Ms Lee Li Lian has obtained 15,800 votes in Punggol East and thereby, she should represent the 15,800 voters who voted for her to be in this House to make a contribution.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: It is illogical because NCMP, by definition, is Non-Constituency Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: An NCMP cannot represent the minority who voted for her in this House.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: So, I do not understand the logic that because she has obtained the votes and, thereby, is "elected".

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: If you want to work the system to say that you wish the minority voters to be represented by MPs, then let us make it equal for all MPs and it should be elected by a proportionate representation system, not our system.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: It is a very different concept from proportionate representation of party lists.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: So, I think let us not try to change the concept and tell people that this is the same.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: This is the way of respecting the wishes of the voters.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Neither is she disrespectful of the Constitution, as the Constitution clearly allows it and precedence also permits for an individual to vacate the NCMP seat.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: So, I do not really understand what the fuss is about.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: It is not a political manoeuvre because it is provided for under the law that says if an NCMP like Ms Lee Li Lian has not taken up the seat, Parliament can decide to fill the vacancy under the law, and hence I moved the Motion to allow Parliament to decide.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Ms Lee Li Lian just told me her application for the use of a venue, a common area, for some function has been rejected by the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: You cannot even have a place to organise activities for the residents.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: That is the difference of being an NCMP.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Even if she accepted the NCMP seat today, I think the outcome will still be the same.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Let us not be hypocrites to say that, "Look, they are the same".

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I know because I have been an elected MP.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: And I see through how the PAP works.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Of course, the rejection is explained as "we do not allow political parties to use common areas ".

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: You use the People's Association (PA), you use Advisers.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: So, it is correct, as NCMP, you cannot sink roots in that way because you just cannot possibly connect with the residents the way you want.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Next, the difference between NCMP and Constituency MP is this: as a constituency MP, you conduct Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS), you represent the residents, you write to the Ministries.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: From the response of the letter, you will know what is the policy and what is the implementation of the policy.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: You can do surveys and thereby, you can air your views in this House, but you will not know exactly the problem and the policy gaps, because you do not get those kinds of cases.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: So, that is fundamentally the difference between constituency MP, elected MP and NCMP.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: You cannot grow muscle because you do not have roots, you are floating.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I have stated why we will reject the amendment because this amendment is not true.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: We do not tell Ms Lee Li Lian, "Look, you don't accept NCMP, and thereby, we can have whoever we like here".

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Mr Leon Perera has given a very good answer.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Yes, you want Singaporeans to believe that there is no need to vote for Opposition.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Just vote for PAP and let us have Opposition members as NCMPs.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: And you are telling them, "Yes, your views will be represented.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I am not saying that it is not useful.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: It can be useful, but fundamentally, this is not what Parliament is for, because Parliament is not a forum to talk shop, or just air views, or spar with Ministers to show that you are a smart guy.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The NCMP scheme can be a drug to Opposition parties, whose candidates may stand for Elections, aiming just to be NCMP, instead of elected MPs.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: This may cause Parliament to become a colosseum in the long run; for the nation to vent their emotions in a show, but with no real consequence.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: As what Ms Sylvia Lim said, "What makes the PAP change?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: What makes the Cabinet shift left?" Not the voice here.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The Workers' Party has been represented in the House since 1981.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Mr Jeyaretnam was the first Opposition Member in 1981.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: If PAP does, I may not need to even move out of Hougang in GE 2011.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I moved out exactly because I realised how much you can talk here, the PAP may not move, because you do not believe what I say.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Your speech will have to be relevant to the Motion.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Yes, so I am talking about the amended Motion?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I can continue with the Motion proper, right?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: The Motion and the amendment are taken together, so you are responding; this is your response.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Because you moved the Motion, so you have the right of reply.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But before you do that, I think we are running out of time.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I have explained earlier, we are a responsible and rational party; we work within the system.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: It is the same: we oppose GRC, but we contested in GRCs.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: And that is the spirit of the Workers' Party in wanting to work the system by respecting the law.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: MPs secure a mandate from the people to make decisions on their behalf in Parliament, thus, representation is the foundation of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Any politician who aspires to enter Parliament must seek and obtain the mandate from the people to represent them so as to seek and effect positive change for the people, not just talk.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: You can air your views, you can debate here, but is there change?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: We have to ask: what are we here for?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Therefore, the NCMP scheme is a distraction from the fundamental meaning of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The NCMP scheme has the potential to anaesthetise Opposition politicians from the consciousness that political conviction is what brings him or her into politics.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Opposition politicians may delude themselves that they are checking the Government when they are, in fact, merely participating in the discussion forum with no real power to effect change.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The NCMP scheme can also inadvertently attract candidates with a different motive and intent to participate in the Elections basically to seek personal fame and glory.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: If such a political culture becomes the predominant phenomenon, we will have bad politics.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: What is more worrying is, should the Ruling party fail one day, what we have left to form an alternative government may be such politicians who have gained exposure and fame through the NCMP route.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: We recognise that having one more NCMP will contribute to the debate and possibly, better policy outcomes.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Hence, it is also meaningful for well-intended individuals who aspire to represent the will of the people to be NCMPs who contribute to the process.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Chan Chun Sing, you have a clarification?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, I fully agree with Mr Low that the NCMP scheme is not a party list scheme.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, I would like to clarify with Mr Low.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: He has mentioned many things that an NCMP cannot do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But why not think about the many things an NCMP can do for this House and for this country?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Third, the People's Association is a Statutory Board under the Government.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It executes the policy and directions for the Government.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Fourth, Mr Leon Perera, you suggested you put yourself at great risk taking up this scheme when you also seem to suggest that this NCMP scheme will endanger the very future of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Why do you want to be a party to this?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And finally, Mr Low, you said you have raised many dangers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, we agree with you there are many changes to the NCMP scheme including people coming in for the wrong reasons, people deluding themselves to showcase.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If these are clear, present dangers, why do you allow your party Members to take up this scheme?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It must be because on balance, you have found this scheme to be useful perhaps not just to yourself but hopefully to the wider Singapore as you have suggested; that they can contribute something even if they are not taking care of a constituency.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Low, you are responding to the clarification?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Yes, we do think there is something to contribute and that is why we allowed individual qualified members to decide whether they want to be NCMP.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: But the NCMP scheme itself is not a scheme which we will support as what we explained many times, that the scheme itself is not going to serve us well.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I am not convinced that this is going to be a scheme that will be able to allow genuine, serious Opposition parties to develop.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I will now put the necessary questions on the Motion for Members' vote.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I will first put the question on the amendment moved by Minister Chan Chun Sing.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Can I have a show of hands on who wants to have their dissent recorded?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Paragraph (c) of the amended Motion, as what I had stated.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Low, I have to explain that the voting is only "yes", or "no", or "abstain" on the entire Motion.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: So, it has to be recorded as either you support or you do not.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But your expressions of disapproval of paragraph (c), that can be recorded.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But you have to be clear whether you support the Motion, or you do not, or you abstain.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: We are at the point where we are voting on the Motion as amended.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: When you vote on the motion as amended, there are only three types of votes that you can cast, either in favour, against, or you abstain.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: So, those are the only votes that will be recorded in terms of how you express it as your votes.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Your opposition or disagreement with paragraph (c) is already recorded earlier on, when we voted on the amendment.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: So, you have to now, make it clear whether you are supporting or you are against or you are abstaining against the Motion as amended.
